definition: The geometry that limits where an analysis runs, such as Bhutan's national boundary or one Dzongkhag.
The Architecture for REDD+ Transactions (ART) and its standard, The REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard (TREES), under which jurisdictions earn emission reduction credits.
High Forest cover, Low Deforestation: jurisdictions with high forest cover and low historical deforestation, which TREES crediting treats differently.
The area of each land-use change (for example hectares of deforestation) over the reference and crediting periods, multiplied by emission factors to give emissions.
An Earth Engine stack of images (ee.ImageCollection), such as all Sentinel-2 scenes, that can be filtered by place, date and metadata.
One image built from many by taking a per-pixel statistic, such as the median, to remove clouds and noise.
An Earth Engine object (ee.Reducer) that summarises many values into one, across images, pixels in a region, or neighbourhoods.
Normalised Difference Vegetation Index, (NIR − Red) / (NIR + Red); higher values mean more green vegetation.
A mask that hides pixels flagged as cloud or cloud shadow so they do not affect composites or classifications.
An input band used by a classifier, such as a spectral band, an index, elevation or slope.
A machine-learning classifier that combines the votes of many decision trees, each trained on a random sample of the data and covariates.
In RLCMS, a probability layer (0–100) for one land-cover class, produced by a classifier and later combined into a map by assemblage rules.
Combining primitives into a single land-cover map with ordered decision-tree rules and thresholds.
Regional Land Cover Monitoring System: the SERVIR primitives-and-assemblage approach to consistent land-cover mapping.
A 64-dimensional vector per 10 m pixel and year (Google's Satellite Embedding dataset, from AlphaEarth Foundations) that summarises the pixel's multi-sensor time series.
A map class used to divide the area for sampling, such as stable forest, stable non-forest or deforestation.
A table that cross-tabulates map classes against reference classes at sample points; the basis of accuracy and area estimates.
The share of samples mapped as a class that really are that class (1 − commission error).
The share of samples that really are a class and were mapped as it (1 − omission error).
The area of a class estimated from the reference sample and the stratum weights (Olofsson et al. 2014), rather than by counting map pixels.
A range expected to contain the true value with a stated probability; TREES reports uncertainty as a 90% confidence interval.
A free web tool for interpreting sample plots on high-resolution imagery, used to label the reference sample.
